questions.question: Which broad area takes the largest share of UK public spending?

options.B: Social protection, including state pensions and benefits

questions.why: HM Treasury PESA consistently shows social protection as the largest function of spending.

questions.question: Roughly how large is total UK public spending compared with the size of the whole economy (GDP)?
questions.why: Total managed expenditure has been roughly 40 to 45 per cent of GDP in recent decades.

questions.question: What is 'debt interest' in government spending?

options.A: Interest the government pays on money it has borrowed

questions.why: Debt interest is the cost of servicing government borrowing.

questions.question: Health spending rose in cash terms but fell 'in real terms'. What does that mean?

options.C: After allowing for rising prices, it bought less than before
options.D: Spending was moved to another department

questions.why: Real terms adjusts cash figures for inflation, so a cash rise can be a real fall.

questions.question: Which single tax raises the most money for the UK government?
questions.why: HMRC and OBR figures show income tax is the largest single source of receipts.

questions.question: Which three taxes together raise more than half of UK government receipts?

options.A: Income tax, National Insurance and VAT
options.B: Fuel duty, stamp duty and council tax
options.C: Corporation tax, inheritance tax and VAT
options.D: Tobacco duty, alcohol duty and air passenger duty

questions.why: Income tax, NICs and VAT are consistently the three biggest revenue sources, together over half of receipts.

questions.question: When the government spends more than it receives in taxes and other receipts, how is the gap mainly covered?

options.B: Borrowing, which adds to public debt
options.C: Cutting the state pension that year

questions.why: The deficit (public sector net borrowing) is financed by borrowing, which is not a tax.

questions.question: Government receipts include more than taxes. Which of these is a non-tax receipt?

options.C: Interest and dividends the government earns on its assets

questions.why: ONS public sector finances count interest, dividends and similar income as receipts that are not taxes.

questions.question: Roughly what share of all income tax is paid by the top 1 per cent of income taxpayers?
questions.why: HMRC distribution statistics show the top 1 per cent pay roughly 25 to 30 per cent of income tax.

questions.question: As a share of their disposable income, how do indirect taxes like VAT compare for the poorest and richest fifth of households?

options.D: The poorest pay no indirect tax

questions.why: ONS Effects of taxes and benefits shows indirect taxes take a larger share of income for poorer households.

questions.question: How do direct taxes, like income tax, change as a share of gross income from poorer to richer households?

options.C: They are zero for all but the richest

questions.why: ONS Effects of taxes and benefits shows direct taxes take a rising share of gross income up the distribution.

questions.question: In official 'who pays' tables, what does 'the poorest fifth of households' mean?

options.A: Households living in the poorest fifth of areas
options.B: The 20 per cent of households with the lowest incomes, after adjusting for household size

questions.why: ONS ranks households into quintiles by equivalised disposable income.

questions.question: Households on average pay about a third of gross income in all taxes. Does that mean the income tax rate is about a third?

options.A: Yes, they are the same thing
options.C: No, it is an average across all taxes, not a personal tax rate
options.D: No, it means a third of households pay tax

questions.why: A household average of all taxes as a share of income differs from a personal rate of one tax.

questions.question: 'Income tax raises about a quarter of all receipts.' What does this tell you?

options.A: People pay a quarter of their income in income tax
options.B: A quarter of people pay income tax
options.C: The basic rate is 25 per cent
options.D: Income tax makes up about a quarter of government revenue

questions.why: A share of total revenue is not a rate paid by individuals or households.

questions.question: Which of these is an indirect tax?
questions.why: VAT is levied on spending, so ONS classes it as indirect; the others are classed as direct.

questions.question: A page shows a clearly labelled 'example household' paying tax. What is it?

options.A: A real family surveyed by ONS
options.C: An illustration to explain the idea, not a measured statistic
options.D: The household that pays the most tax

questions.why: Illustrations show how calculations work and must be kept separate from measured figures.

questions.question: The headline UK employment rate usually refers to people in which age group?
questions.why: ONS Labour Force Survey headline employment rate covers people aged 16 to 64.

questions.question: Job categories changed from one official occupation classification to another. What should a chart do across that point?

options.B: Show the break clearly and warn that the categories are not directly comparable
options.D: Drop the older years without saying so

questions.why: Classification changes (e.g. SOC 2010 to SOC 2020) create breaks in the series that must be shown.

questions.question: Average pay rose 4 per cent in cash terms while prices rose 6 per cent. What happened to real pay?
questions.why: Real pay is cash pay adjusted for inflation, so a 4 per cent rise against 6 per cent inflation is a fall.

questions.question: In England, which is the most common housing tenure?
questions.why: The English Housing Survey shows roughly two thirds of households are owner occupiers.

questions.question: Private renting grew a lot in England after 2000. What does that chart alone show?

options.C: The change, but not on its own what caused it

questions.why: A trend shows what changed; it does not by itself prove the cause.

questions.question: Which country is the most visited overseas destination for UK residents?
questions.why: ONS Travel trends consistently shows Spain as the top destination for UK residents' visits abroad.

questions.question: Official travel survey data are missing for part of the pandemic. How should those years be shown?

options.B: Filled in from the years either side
options.D: As a clearly marked gap with an explanation

questions.why: The International Passenger Survey was suspended in 2020, so years are missing, not zero.

questions.question: In England, what is the legal maximum class size for infant classes (ages 5 to 7) with one teacher?
questions.why: The School Admissions (Infant Class Sizes) regulations limit infant classes in England to 30 pupils per teacher.
